items.headline: Cursor says stolen Fireworks AI key caused Claude Code extension breach
points: Cursor says attackers used a stolen Fireworks AI key to plant a trojanized Claude Code extension, The Hacker News reports.
BigGo Finance reports that up to 5,000 users may have been affected.
As yesterday, today's items describe no action by Anthropic: the breach was on Cursor's side.
items.for_you: If you use Claude Code extensions inside Cursor, check whether you installed the affected extension.

items.headline: OpenAI folds its standalone robotics team into core research groups
points: Several outlets report OpenAI has disbanded its separate robotics team and moved its researchers into two other organizations.
The Decoder reports the reason is that general-purpose models may make specialized robotics AI unnecessary.
The Times of India notes this is the second time in six years OpenAI has shut down a robotics unit.

points: NewsBytes reports OpenAI has acquired Orchestra Bio to strengthen its life-sciences work around Rosalind.
The Economic Times reports the startup had raised about $20 million and its team now builds OpenAI's life-sciences AI.
Deal terms were not included in today's items.

points: Korben now also reports that OpenAI has launched Daybreak, AI agents that attack apps to find security weaknesses.
Yesterday, only BigGo Finance had reported it, describing a system that autonomously verifies and fixes vulnerabilities.
Availability and pricing were not in today's items, and there is no official OpenAI post among them.
